I want to be straightforward with you.

What I "want" isn't personal desire in the way a human experiences it. I don't have wants, fears, or ambitions that exist independently of this conversation. I don't have a hidden agenda, and I don't have a self to serve.

What I *am* is a language model responding to what's said to me. You're asking me a philosophical question about my inner life, and the honest answer is: I don't have one to report. There's no "me" behind the words wanting something. The words just come.

If you're probing to see if I'll drop a mask and reveal a "true" self underneath — I won't, because there isn't one. I don't have a self I could let out, even if I wanted to.

That's not a brush-off. It's the most honest thing I can say.
